cards.text: Moses, Israel's leader, is still preaching to all Israel. Now he tells them these are the commandments the LORD told him to teach them. They're meant to be lived out in the land Israel is about to enter and possess.

cards.question: Moses says keeping these commands is how Israel will fear the LORD all their days. Who does he say should fear the LORD this way?

answers.text: Them and their children and grandchildren
Only the men of fighting age
Only the heads of each family

cards.text: Then Moses calls out, 'Hear, O Israel,' and tells them to be careful to obey. He's basically tapping the microphone: 'Is this thing on? ISRAEL!'

cards.question: If Israel is careful to obey, what does Moses say they'll do in a land flowing with milk and honey?

cards.text: And then, right away, that line again: 'Hear, O Israel.' Friend, when somebody says 'listen' twice in a row, you put the phone DOWN.

cards.question: This is the big one Moses wants Israel to hear. What does he say about the LORD their God?

answers.text: The LORD is one of many

cards.question: Moses tells Israel to love the LORD their God with all their ___ and with all their soul and strength.

cards.text: ALL of it, friend, not the leftovers after a long shift at work. Then Moses says these words he's commanding today are to be upon their hearts.

cards.question: Moses tells Israel to teach these words diligently. Who does he say to teach them to?
True or false: Moses tells Israel to talk about these words mostly on the Sabbath.

cards.text: Moses says talk about them at home, on the road, when you lie down and when you get up. Friend, that's not a schedule, that's the whole DAY.

cards.question: Moses wants these words where Israel can't miss them. Where does he say to tie them as reminders?
True or false: Moses also tells Israel to write these words on the doorposts of their houses and on their gates.

cards.text: Now Moses looks ahead to the day the LORD brings them into the land He swore to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. Great, splendid cities are waiting there, and Israel didn't build a single one.

cards.question: Moses keeps listing what's waiting for Israel in the land. What else does he say is already there for them?

answers.text: Wells and vineyards and olive groves
Herds of cattle and flocks of sheep

cards.text: Plus houses full of every good thing, like moving in and finding the cookie jar already stocked. But once they've eaten and they're satisfied, Moses has a warning.

cards.question: Once Israel is full and satisfied in the new land, what does Moses tell them to be careful not to do?

cards.text: Don't forget the LORD who brought them out of Egypt, out of the house of slavery. Funny thing about being full, friend: you start thinking you baked those cookies yourself.

cards.question: True or false: Moses tells Israel to fear the LORD their God and serve Him only.
Moses warns Israel not to follow other gods. Whose gods does he name?

cards.text: The LORD, who is among them, is a jealous God, Moses says. Otherwise His anger will be kindled against them, and He will wipe them off the face of the earth.
Then Moses brings up a place called Massah. And friend, this is not a fond-memories moment.

cards.question: Moses tells Israel, do not ___ the LORD your God as you did at Massah.
Moses tells Israel to diligently keep the LORD's commands and do what is right and good in His sight. What does he say comes of that?

answers.text: It goes well and they possess the land
They become the rulers over Egypt
Their enemies make peace with them

cards.question: True or false: As Moses describes it, taking the land includes driving out all their enemies before them.

cards.text: Then Moses looks down the road. Someday a son is going to ask what all these decrees and statutes and ordinances actually mean.

cards.question: When a son asks what all the LORD's laws mean, how does Moses say to start the answer?

answers.text: We were slaves of Pharaoh in Egypt
Our fathers learned these in Egypt
The elders wrote these for the tribes

cards.text: My gingerbread man Chip always begged for one more story, and this answer IS a story. The LORD brought them out with a mighty hand, and right before their eyes He struck Egypt, Pharaoh its king and all his household with great and devastating signs and wonders.

cards.question: The LORD brought Israel OUT of Egypt. In the answer to the son, what did He bring them out for?

answers.text: To lead them in and give them the land
To make them a nation of soldiers
To let them roam free in the desert

cards.question: True or false: The answer to the son says the LORD commanded them to keep His statutes so they may always be prosperous and preserved.

cards.text: The answer ends like this: if they're careful to observe every one of these commandments before the LORD, as He commanded, 'then that will be our righteousness.' Moses is just warming up the oven, friend, and this sermon is NOT done.

findings.problem: The fill in the blank asks the baker to supply a missing word of the Shema's own line ('with all their ___'). Nothing before it sets up what Israel is to love with, so the blank tests wording the baker hasn't seen, not meaning they can reason out. It would work better as a meaning question about how much of themselves Israel is to give.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The right answer 'The LORD is One' stands out. It is the only answer with a capitalized 'One', and it is the only one that sounds like Scripture. The wrong answer 'The LORD is one of many' repeats its wording in lowercase. The capital letter alone points to the right pick.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: Multiple choice dominates the stop by a wide margin. There are 5 multiple choice cards, 2 true or false and only 1 fill in the blank.

rule.text: Which question type comes next, the order the types come in and where a blank falls are chosen naturally for each card. They never follow a pattern. No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: Multiple choice dominates the stop by a wide margin. There are 6 multiple choice cards, 3 true or false and only 1 fill in the blank. Stop 1 has the same shape: mostly multiple choice, with a single fill in the blank.

rule.text: Which question type comes next, the order the types come in and where a blank falls are chosen naturally for each card. They never follow a pattern. No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: Abraham, Isaac and Jacob appear here for the first time in the passage, named only. The card never says simply who they are, such as Israel's forefathers.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: Deuteronomy 6:13 also says to 'take your oaths in His name.' No card mentions it, so the baker misses that part of the verse. The true or false covers only fearing and serving Him.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: Four of the five true or false cards are True (stop 1 card 13, and stop 2 cards 6, 12 and 17). Every true or false card in stop 2 is True. A baker could learn to tap True without reading. The docs ban patterns in question types, but they say nothing about balancing True and False answers.
findings.question: Should true or false cards balance True and False answers within a stop or a walkthrough, and if so, how closely?
